assumptions: The credential sweep in #90 covered repository history, dangling objects and the working tree, as its body states. If the method is narrower than that, say so — the finding depends on its scope.
constraints: This is the batch's one process command. Documentation only. $0.00. No code, test, run or key.

SUPERSEDE D31 BY QUOTATION — do not delete it. Record that its PREMISE was wrong, not merely that it went stale: D31 assumed an exposure existed and had been remediated. A full sweep of history, dangling objects and the tree found no credential at all. The warning was authored by an advisory agent that misread something; it was never true.

RULING D32, COMMITTED VERBATIM: 'Ruling D32 — an assertion about a security exposure is a measurement or it is not written. HANDOVER section 3.6 carried an ACTION REQUIRED naming two GitHub PATs and three OpenRouter keys, authored by an advisory agent that inferred it rather than measuring it. A sweep of the full repository history, dangling objects and the tree returned negative: no credential was ever exposed. The warning was not stale, it was untrue. Two consequences. First, an unverified security warning is worse than no warning, because it burns the credibility of every later one and it invites a remediation that cannot be performed. Second, the warning was propagated as fact for a week by a reader who had no way to distinguish it from a measurement — including by the advisor, who reported it as an outstanding owner failure and wrote a ruling (D31) on its premise. A security claim must name the artefact it inspected, the method, and the result, so a reader can see it was computed. D31 is superseded and retained as the exhibit of a ruling built on an unmeasured claim.'

RECORD THE ADVISOR'S ERROR EXPLICITLY, attributed to the advisor, and record the pattern: this is the fourth instance of the same failure in one session — a document claim read as a measured fact. The others: the HANDOVER HEAD stamp, the '42-call ceiling' reading of the B14 run, and Ruling D20's premise. State the pattern plainly. Do not soften it and do not attribute it to the earlier advisory model alone: the advisor propagated it after the owner said the keys were rotated, and wrote an accusatory line about a failure that did not exist.

RECORD THE TECHNICAL-SET RUN, and record it carefully so it is not read as a clean validation. Items 2 (tech-pool-sizing) and 7 (tech-backfill-migration) were run: pool BLOCKED at 42 calls and $0.49; backfill ESCALATED at $0.31. The advisor graded both SEVERE(5) and HIGH(4) in the difficulty table — but stated them as ESTIMATES with an explicit caveat that they should be measured rather than trusted, so this is a SOFT agreement and must be labelled one. Do not claim a prediction held.

RECORD THE CAPABILITY FINDING, which is the real result: a live run on a high-cardinality constraint reached a terminal (BLOCKED) but did not converge, and a comparator produced the arithmetic the harness did not. State that this is a capability limit, not a defect, and that it sits on the cardinality class ARCH-20260922-037 measured — 25 of 26 criteria the classifier called computable were not computable by a counter.

RECORD THAT ARCH-20260925-067 HAS STILL NEVER FIRED LIVE. 084 shipped and pool blocked before review; no run has returned review ship:false with a rework cycle. The fix remains proven provider-free only, and the condition that would exercise it is named: a run that reaches review and is sent back. Do not open a command for this; record the condition.
Do NOT open any ledger row. Do NOT change code, tests or workflows. Do NOT issue a new guard. If you believe a guard is required for any of this, return the question rather than writing one.
Every count re-derived against the tree (convention 24). Suite reported before and after.
